counterfactual_missing_items: No family history of HHT or recurrent epistaxis
No definite vascular malformation on abdominal ultrasound
No telangiectasias at characteristic HHT sites such as lips, oral mucosa, or fingertips
decisive_items: repeated right-sided epistaxis without obvious trauma
Multiple small capillary malformations on trunk (hyperpigmented)
response.rationale: R1 is the strongest because recurrent unilateral epistaxis, progressive anemia, and nasal endoscopy showing a vascular malformation with capillary dilation form a coherent HHT pattern. R5 has facial erythema and seizures but lacks leptomeningeal angiomatosis on cranial CT; R3 lacks limb overgrowth; R2 and R4 lack their defining systemic features.

rejected.why: No large facial hemangioma, posterior fossa malformation, arterial anomaly, or ocular finding required for PHACE syndrome.
No limb hypertrophy or varicosities; capillary malformations and a nasal vascular lesion are not specific to Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome.
No skin hyperextensibility, joint hypermobility, or connective tissue fragility; normal coagulation and a localized vascular malformation do not support Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
